text: Limburger ripens mainly from the outside: a smear of yeasts followed by coryneform bacteria such as Brevibacterium linens grows on the surface and drives the breakdown of the paste. Rubbing closes surface openings and spreads these organisms over the whole block.

links.name: El-Erian, Bacteriological studies on Limburger cheese (Wageningen, 1969)

sources.text: The table, the facts and the words on how it is made, from these.

steps.note: The curd is put into wooden forms and cut into blocks of about 250 g.
The surface is smeared with yeasts, then bacteria, which grow on it and break the paste down from outside.
The cheese ripens in high humidity and is rubbed a few times.
